claims.text: The onset and progression of the phase transition in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles are governed by surface-initiated premelting.
Local atomic-scale compositional heterogeneities exist at particular nanoparticle surface sites.
Surface compositional heterogeneities locally lower the melting point.
The lower-melting surface sites nucleate structural disordering.
A disordered or liquid-like surface layer forms before the nanoparticle core melts.
The premelted surface layer forms below the bulk melting temperature.
The premelted layer propagates inward as temperature increases.
In-situ imaging should reveal a liquid-like or amorphous surface layer before complete core melting.
Calorimetry should show an initial endothermic event associated with surface premelting.
The surface-premelting event should be followed by a larger endothermic event associated with complete melting.
The timing and extent of the endothermic transitions should correlate with particle size or surface area.
Particle size influences the initiation temperature or extent of surface premelting.
The starting nanoparticles are solid and crystalline, with nominally homogeneous FeNiCrCoCu composition and no room-temperature surface disorder.
Oxidation or other environmental changes may alter the surface chemistry and cause deviations from the proposed behavior.
The proposed behavior applies under inert, high-vacuum conditions but may differ for substantially different particle sizes.
Absence of a distinct surface-initiated premelting layer before complete melting would falsify the hypothesis.
